source_version_rechecked: Abiad-Castriota, arXiv:2607.13666v1, 2026-07-15; still the only version listed at this checkpoint
full_target: Exact incidence-corrected (4,2) counting in cubic binary Tanner graphs without four-cycles, with a formula in cyclic socket data using the full evaluated rectangular matrix and standard complex DFT. The combined canonical question also includes (4,0), outside this block.
conclusion: The complete-STS (4,2) count is classical (1995). Expanded-graph ETS enumeration, shared-six-cycle/theta structure and modular QC avoidance are established prior work. No earlier complete incidence-corrected QC socket/Fourier support formula was identified in the inspected versions. The expanded chordless-cycle journal text and named other full texts remain unresolved comparisons; no priority claim is established.

sources.title: A Small Basis for Four-Line Configurations in Steiner Triple Systems
sources.date_or_version: 1995 journal article, author-hosted accepted preprint inspected
sources.locator: Figure 2 (PDF page 5), C14 derivation (PDF page 6), formula summary (PDF page 10)
sources.relationship: The C14 pattern has four triples, five degree-two points and two degree-one points; it is exactly the elementary (4,2) Tanner pattern. The stated count is v(v-1)(v-3)/4 - 6P, where P is the Pasch count.
sources.comparison_limit: Requires every pair of check-points to occur in exactly one triple: a complete STS(v). Arbitrary linear cubic socket incidences do not satisfy this. The 1995 result already supplies the STS special case and implies loss of count information from the common STS point-Gram matrix; neither observation is claimed as new here. The source-to-pattern labels are a written diagram translation, supported by a concrete Lean shape certificate.

sources.title: Algorithms and Complexity for Counting Configurations in Steiner Triple Systems
sources.relationship: Theorem 3 gives O(v^3) counting for every variable four-line STS configuration, using the 1995 reduction to Pasch counts. Counting and listing complexity are explicitly distinguished.
sources.comparison_limit: A complete STS is the input. This establishes a strong earlier counting result for that special case; it is not the arbitrary cyclic socket Fourier identity.

sources.title: Counting Configurations in Designs
sources.date_or_version: Indexed author preprint dated 1997-08-21; journal 2001, JCTA 96(2), 341-357
sources.access: Relevant indexed primary preprint passages read; full 2001 journal PDF opened in the normal publisher browser; whole-file comparison incomplete after download-tool stall.
sources.locator: Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2/proof (indexed page 5), Corollary 3.3 (page 8), Theorem 5.1/proof (page 10)
sources.relationship: General t-design reduction must be checked, because a check-regular cubic incidence structure is a 1-design. A generator has more than t repeated points in every block. C14 is a generator for t=1 and a non-generator for t=2, as verified in ClassicalConfiguration.lean.
sources.comparison_limit: Theorem 5.1 reduces non-generators and therefore does not compute the general 1-design C14 count from other generator counts. Complete STS inputs have t=2 and admit the classical reduction. The named preprint passages were inspected. The final 17-page journal PDF opened through the publisher open-archive link, but download failures prevented completing the final-text comparison in this block.

sources.title: Graphical Analysis of Lifted Product Code Constructions
sources.relationship: Rechecked the base-configuration counts and lifting mechanism against the present target.
sources.comparison_limit: Theorem 4.4 counts absorbing patterns in the monomial base graph; Corollary 4.5 treats the lifts of its two-variable zero-syndrome patterns via cycle order. These are not the complete elementary (4,2) count in arbitrary expanded QC-GHP socket incidences. The shared equal-base product setting also differs from the one-factor-scalar QC-GHP form here.

sources.title: Trapping Sets of Detector Error Models
sources.locator: Sections III.1-III.3; Appendix B, including dot expansion and complete exhaustive-search procedure
sources.relationship: New forward-citation lead. Uses established dpl enumeration on full detector Tanner graphs, followed by decoder-specific fault tests. In a cubic no-four-cycle graph its LETS catalog includes the (4,2) elementary supports.
sources.comparison_limit: This is an earlier general enumeration approach, not a new claim of ours. It does not supply the inspected socket/Fourier identity; its detector matrices and decoder experiments have a different scope from the present incidence theorem.

sources.title: Construction of Protograph-Based LDPC Codes With Chordless Short Cycles
sources.date_or_version: arXiv:2008.01322v1, 2020-08-04; expanded journal version online 2023-08-22, IEEE TIT 70(1), 51-74, January 2024
sources.locator: Preprint Definition 2; Figure 1; Section IV, Theorems 6-7/proofs and multi-edge subsection IV-B; final journal abstract/metadata
sources.relationship: Close predecessor: a chorded eight-cycle has a diamond normal graph, and the preprint uses paired six-cycle equations with common socket data to avoid it. Its stated scope includes single-edge and multi-edge, regular and irregular protographs; it cannot be excluded merely by assuming three fully occupied row groups.
sources.comparison_limit: The inspected criteria detect/avoid configurations rather than give the separate incidence-corrected (4,2) support count with Fourier normalization. The shared-six-cycle/modular detection idea is prior work. Eight-page preprint and 24-page journal article are different versions; a complete comparison with the expanded journal remains an access gap.

sources.title: Efficient Search of QC-LDPC Codes with Girths 6 and 8 and Free of Elementary Trapping Sets with Small Size
sources.locator: Sections II-III, difference matrices D/DD, Theorem 1 and proof; Figure 2
sources.relationship: Earlier sufficient modular conditions eliminate (4,0) and (4,2) ETSs in fully connected (3,n)-regular single-edge QC codes by eliminating selected eight-cycles.
sources.comparison_limit: Uses three fully occupied check-row groups and gives avoidance conditions. It is not an exact arbitrary sparse/multiple-edge QC socket count or its complex Fourier formula. Those restrictions apply to this 2018 preprint, not to the broader 2020/2024 chordless-cycle work.

sources.title: Theoretical Bounds for the Size of Elementary Trapping Sets by Graphic Methods
sources.locator: Section III, theta Turan number; Section IV-A, Theorem 7/proof; Section V construction discussion
sources.relationship: The diamond is theta(1,2,2) in the normal graph. Exact Turan bounds yield ETS size bounds under a condition excluding shared short cycles.
sources.comparison_limit: Counts extremal edges or classifies possible sizes after exclusion; it does not count embeddings of (4,2) supports in a given QC incidence. The inspected version is the 2023 v1 preprint.

sources.title: The Impact of the Distance Between Cycles on Elementary Trapping Sets
sources.date_or_version: arXiv:2503.01341v1, 2025-03-03; journal DOI 10.1109/TIT.2025.3631564 recorded as a separate publication milestone, not inspected full text
sources.locator: Definitions 1-4; Sections III-B and IV; Example 1 (explicit (4,2) system matrix); enumeration tables
sources.relationship: Studies theta/dumbbell cycle overlaps, ETS sizes and the spectral radius of the decoder state-space system matrix. Includes an explicit (4,2) model.
sources.comparison_limit: Its spectral matrix is the local message-propagation matrix, not the evaluated check Gram M_j. Its counts of nonisomorphic shapes differ from the number of supports in a specified socket graph. No exact target Fourier identity was identified in the inspected preprint.

sources.title: Turan-Theoretic Bounds on Several Elementary Trapping Sets in LDPC Codes
sources.locator: Definitions; Section IV, Theorems 6-7 and derivation from extremal graph bounds; Section V-A, tables of nonisomorphic ETSs and system spectral radii
sources.relationship: Forward-citation follow-up studies forbidden cycle overlaps, Turan numbers and ETS size bounds, with catalogs of nonisomorphic shapes and local system spectral radii.
sources.comparison_limit: The inspected counts are shape catalogs, not embeddings in a specified QC code. Theorems 6-7 bound sizes under extra forbidden-subgraph hypotheses; they do not give the general incidence-corrected Fourier support count.

sources.title: On a class of column-weight 3 decomposable LDPC codes with the analysis of elementary trapping sets
sources.access: Relevant full primary PDF sections/proofs inspected in first block; row-partition definition rechecked in the indexed primary page in this block
sources.locator: Definition of decomposability (p586); Section5 pp590–592, Proposition5.5, Theorem3 and proof, Algorithm1, Table5; QC-lift setup Section6
sources.relationship: Rechecked the three-check-group hypothesis and distinguished normal-graph shape enumeration from support counts in a given code.
sources.comparison_limit: The 168-column witnesses contain a Fano block and cannot admit three check groups; the smaller 48-column pair does admit this partition, using check coordinate modulo 3. Algorithm 1 enumerates nonisomorphic shapes rather than embeddings. These distinctions do not exclude the broader arbitrary-protograph chordless-cycle literature. Concrete Fano exclusion and finite three-group checks are provided by this follow-up at their separately labeled evidence levels.

sources.title: Switching graphs and designs
sources.locator: Introduction; Section 3, Theorem 3.2 and proof; Section 4.2, Theorems 4.3-4.4 and proofs
sources.relationship: Source-author downstream paper: extends CS-switching to divisible designs and relates design switching to cospectral graph switching. The proof of Theorem 3.2 preserves point-pair incidence counts.
sources.comparison_limit: These are parameter-preserving transformations, not a computation of (4,2) support multiplicities or their Fourier formula. Gram-preserving design switches are relevant prior machinery, not claimed new here. The inspected theorem comparison goes beyond keyword absence.

sources.title: High-rate quantum low-density parity-check codes assisted by reliable qubits
sources.locator: Sections III-B/C, Proposition 3.7, Theorems 3.9-3.15; Section IV final STS comparison; Section V Theorem 5.1/proof; references 60 and 77
sources.relationship: Closed citation lead after correcting the unavailable v3 request to the actual latest v2. Even configurations control distance; assisted-code constructions and finite-geometry bounds are prior work.
sources.comparison_limit: Even-freeness excludes zero-odd-point supports; it does not count two-odd-point supports. The cited bounds and assisted-code constructions do not supply the general QC socket multiplicity identity. Section IV refers its small-configuration analysis to the still-unavailable Laendner-Milenkovic-Huber 2010 paper; this is not a substitute for that full text.
